chart.note: Original simplified redraw of the area around Livermore, not the FAA chart. Frequencies and numbers are illustrative: check the current sectional and Chart Supplement.

hotspots.name: Towered airport
hotspots.legend: Blue airport symbol with runways drawn inside
hotspots.explanation: Blue means the airport has a control tower. The runway layout is drawn inside the circle for hard-surfaced runways between 1,500 and 8,069 ft. The small ticks around the edge mean fuel and services are available.

hotspots.name: Airport data block
hotspots.explanation: Name and identifier; CT is the control tower frequency (the star means it is part-time) and ATIS is the recorded weather. The last line gives the field elevation (400 ft), L for runway lighting, the longest runway in hundreds of feet (5,300 ft) and the UNICOM frequency.

hotspots.name: Class D boundary
hotspots.explanation: The Class D airspace around a towered airport. Establish two-way radio contact with the tower before you cross this line.

hotspots.name: Class D ceiling
hotspots.legend: Number in a dashed blue box
hotspots.explanation: The top of the Class D in hundreds of feet MSL: 29 means 2,900 ft. A minus sign in front (−29) would mean up to but not including 2,900 ft.

hotspots.name: Class B floor and ceiling
hotspots.explanation: In this part of the Class B the airspace starts at 4,000 ft MSL and goes up to 10,000 ft MSL (hundreds of feet). Below 4,000 ft you are outside Class B.

hotspots.name: Class B boundary
hotspots.explanation: The edge of a Class B shelf. Inside it, between the floor and ceiling, you need an ATC clearance.

hotspots.name: Class E from 700 ft
hotspots.explanation: Inside the fuzzy side of the band, Class E starts 700 ft above the ground instead of 1,200 ft. It marks airports with instrument approaches.

hotspots.name: Non-towered airport
hotspots.explanation: Magenta means there is no control tower. Announce your position and intentions on the CTAF shown in the data block.

hotspots.name: CTAF
hotspots.explanation: At a non-towered airport the frequency marked with a C in a circle is the Common Traffic Advisory Frequency (CTAF): use it for your position reports.

hotspots.name: Private airport
hotspots.explanation: A private (restricted) airport: use only in an emergency or with the owner's permission.

hotspots.name: Maximum elevation figure (MEF)
hotspots.legend: Large blue number with a smaller one: 3⁶
hotspots.explanation: The highest terrain or obstacle in this latitude-longitude box, rounded up: 3⁶ means 3,600 ft MSL. Stay above it and you clear everything in the box.

hotspots.name: Obstacle
hotspots.explanation: The top of the obstacle is 1,520 ft MSL (bold) and 620 ft above the ground (in brackets). Towers can have guy wires spreading far from the tower.

hotspots.name: VORTAC
hotspots.legend: Compass rose around a VORTAC symbol
hotspots.explanation: A VOR navigation station (a VORTAC also has military TACAN). The compass rose shows magnetic directions from the station, so you can read radials straight off the chart.

hotspots.name: VOR information box
hotspots.explanation: The station's name, frequency and three-letter identifier. Tune the frequency and check the Morse code identifier before you use it.

hotspots.name: Victor airway
hotspots.explanation: A low-altitude airway between VORs, from 1,200 ft above the ground up to 17,999 ft. It is Class E airspace.

hotspots.name: Isogonic line
hotspots.explanation: Magnetic variation along this line is 14° east. Subtract east variation to turn a true course into a magnetic course (east is least).

hotspots.name: Highway
hotspots.legend: Double line with a route shield
hotspots.explanation: A good landmark for pilotage: big roads are easy to see from the air and easy to match to the chart.

hotspots.name: Railroad
hotspots.explanation: Another landmark. Railroads run in long straight lines and gentle curves.

hotspots.name: Built-up area
hotspots.explanation: The shape of a town or city as it looks from the air, especially at night. Keep at least 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle over congested areas.

hotspots.name: Lake
hotspots.explanation: Open water is one of the best landmarks: its shape is easy to recognize.
